Description: Required hostnames are configured on all seven nodes.
RunFrom: sh-edge-a6, sh-user-a6, sz-edge-a6, ops-a6, services-a6, directory-a6 and network-a6
Commands: Source: each node. Run `hostname`. Expected: exact hostname assigned to that role.
ExpectedResult: sh-edge-a6, sh-user-a6, sz-edge-a6, ops-a6, services-a6, directory-a6, network-a6.

Description: Static network configuration and default gateways are correct and persistent.
Commands: Source: gateways and servers. Run `ip -br -4 addr`, `ip route`; inspect the active persistent network backend. Restart the network service only if safe. Expected: exact addresses/prefixes and required default routes, no unintended default route.
ExpectedResult: All gateway/server IPv4 addresses match the task. services-a6 default via 10.76.30.1; directory-a6 and network-a6 default via 10.76.40.1. Configuration survives service restart/reboot.

Description: Both client addresses are obtained by DHCP, not statically configured.
Commands: Source: both clients. Run `ip -4 addr`; inspect network profile and DHCP lease state. Expected: reserved address present and no static address workaround.
ExpectedResult: sh-user-a6=10.76.10.100 and ops-a6=10.76.20.100; persistent client profile uses DHCP.

Description: IPv4 forwarding and private routing are configured on both site gateways.
Commands: Source: sh-edge-a6 and sz-edge-a6. Run `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward` and `ip route`. Expected: forwarding=1 and required routes present.
ExpectedResult: net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 persistently. Each gateway has routes required for its local/private networks.

Description: WireGuard addressing, endpoints and AllowedIPs match the task.
Commands: Source: both gateways. Run `ip -4 addr show wg0` and `wg show`. Expected: exact tunnel addresses, endpoint/listen port, and restricted AllowedIPs.
ExpectedResult: wg0: 10.200.6.1/30 and 10.200.6.2/30; endpoint uses peer WAN address and UDP/51820; AllowedIPs contain only remote private prefixes; 0.0.0.0/0 is absent.

Description: WireGuard tunnel is operational and automatically starts.
Commands: Source: sh-edge-a6. Send traffic to 10.200.6.2, then immediately run `wg show`. Expected: latest handshake <=120 seconds. On both gateways run `systemctl is-active wg-quick@wg0` and `systemctl is-enabled wg-quick@wg0`; both succeed.
ExpectedResult: A fresh handshake is produced on demand and wg-quick@wg0 is active/enabled.

Description: Shanghai-to-Shenzhen private application traffic uses wg0.
Commands: Source: sh-edge-a6. Run `ip route get 10.76.30.10` and `ip route get 10.76.40.20`. Expected: route via wg0. Confirm one private service connection from sh-user-a6 while observing `tcpdump -ni wg0`.
ExpectedResult: Routes to Shenzhen private prefixes use WireGuard; public WAN destination is not used for private service access.

Description: Kea scopes, reservations and options match the task.
Commands: Source: network-a6. Run `kea-dhcp4 -t /etc/kea/kea-dhcp4.conf` and inspect the loaded config. Expected: valid config with both scopes/reservations/options exactly as specified.
ExpectedResult: Pools: 10.76.10.110-149 and 10.76.20.110-149. Reservations: .100 for sh-user/ops. Options: correct router, DNS 10.76.40.10 + 10.76.40.20, domain nova.a6.test.

Description: DHCP relay and real renew/rebind work on both sites.
Commands: Source: gateways/network-a6/clients. On sh-edge-a6 run `ip route get 10.76.40.20` -> wg0. Restart Kea, perform a real DHCP renew/rebind on both clients, then re-check address, default route, both DNS servers and search domain. Expected: all values restored correctly.
ExpectedResult: Both gateways relay DHCP; Shanghai relay reaches network-a6 through wg0. After Kea restart, both clients renew/rebind and retain reservations/options.
Notes: Do not award for a client that merely retains an old lease without a real renew/rebind.

Description: Primary authoritative DNS contains the complete required forward-zone data.
Commands: Source: internal client. Query directory-a6 directly with `dig` for SOA/NS, every required A record, MX and `_ldap._tcp` SRV. Expected: authoritative answers and exact values. This aspect is all-or-nothing; use B1.02/B1.03 for separate secondary/reverse checks.
ExpectedResult: directory-a6 is authoritative for nova.a6.test. Required host A records, aliases/public-style names, MX and LDAP SRV return the task-defined values.

Description: Secondary authoritative DNS is loaded and synchronized.
Commands: Source: network-a6. Run `dig @127.0.0.1 nova.a6.test SOA +noall +answer +comments` and compare serial with primary. Expected: authoritative response and matching serial.
ExpectedResult: network-a6 serves nova.a6.test as secondary with the same SOA serial as directory-a6.

Description: Required reverse zones and PTR records are correct.
Commands: Source: internal client. Run `dig -x` for 10.76.10.100, 10.76.20.100, 10.76.30.10, 10.76.40.10, 10.76.40.20 against the authoritative DNS servers. Expected: correct FQDN PTR values.
ExpectedResult: PTR records exist for sh-user-a6, ops-a6, services-a6, directory-a6 and network-a6 and are served authoritatively.

Description: Zone transfer policy is correct.
Commands: Source: network-a6 and ops-a6. Run `dig AXFR nova.a6.test @10.76.40.10`. Expected: success from network-a6, REFUSED/failed from ops-a6.
ExpectedResult: AXFR from network-a6 to directory-a6 succeeds; AXFR from an ordinary client is denied.

Description: Recursive service is permitted internally and denied from WAN source.
Commands: Internal source: run `dig @10.76.40.10 example.invalid A +recurse`. Expected: any legitimate resolver result/status except REFUSED. WAN source: on sz-edge-a6 run `dig -b 198.18.76.20 @10.76.40.10 example.invalid A +recurse`. Expected: REFUSED/recursion denied. Internet success is not required.
ExpectedResult: Internal recursive requests are not REFUSED; a source bound to Shenzhen WAN 198.18.76.20 is denied recursion.

Description: Both DHCP clients use both internal DNS servers and the required search domain.
Commands: Source: sh-user-a6 and ops-a6. Run `resolvectl status` or the equivalent resolver-state command. Expected: both DNS servers and search domain on both clients.
ExpectedResult: Resolver state contains 10.76.40.10, 10.76.40.20 and nova.a6.test.

Description: Client name resolution survives primary DNS failure without configuration changes.
Commands: Source: expert-controlled test. Stop bind9 on directory-a6, flush client resolver cache, then run `getent ahostsv4 portal.nova.a6.test` on sh-user-a6. Expected: 10.76.30.10. Restart bind9 and verify active state before continuing.
ExpectedResult: With bind9 stopped on directory-a6, an internal client still resolves an internal FQDN through network-a6.

Subsection: OpenLDAP, PKI and SSSD identity services
Description: LDAP directory structure, users, groups, IDs and memberships are correct.
Commands: Source: directory-a6. Use privileged `ldapsearch` or `slapcat` for People/Groups. Expected: exact DNs, uidNumber/gidNumber and memberships.
ExpectedResult: Suffix/OU structure exists. maya UID 8601; timur UID 8602. linuxusers GID 7600; filewriters GID 7601; webadmins GID 7610. Membership matches the task.

Subsection: OpenLDAP, PKI and SSSD identity services
Description: ldap-reader can bind and perform required read/search operations.
Commands: Source: ops-a6 or another trusted client. Run `ldapwhoami -x -ZZ` and a targeted `ldapsearch -ZZ` using ldap-reader with trusted CA. Expected: successful bind and readable permitted attributes.
ExpectedResult: uid=ldap-reader,ou=Services,... authenticates using Reader39@A6 and can read/search identity/group attributes.

Subsection: OpenLDAP, PKI and SSSD identity services
Description: ldap-reader cannot modify directory data.
Commands: Source: directory-a6/ops-a6. Attempt to modify only the `description` attribute of `uid=timur,ou=People,...` using ldap-reader. Expected: `Insufficient access (50)` or equivalent; immediately query the entry and confirm the attribute was not changed.
ExpectedResult: Write access is denied without changing the directory.

Subsection: OpenLDAP, PKI and SSSD identity services
Description: Anonymous LDAP access is restricted to safe RootDSE information.
Commands: Source: client. Run anonymous base search on `-b '' -s base`, then anonymous search under `ou=People,...` requesting `uid,userPassword`. Expected: RootDSE readable; protected directory/password data not disclosed.
ExpectedResult: Anonymous RootDSE base query succeeds. Anonymous browsing of ou=People and reading password attributes is denied/returns no protected data.

Subsection: OpenLDAP, PKI and SSSD identity services
Description: LDAP StartTLS certificate chain and SAN validation are correct.
Commands: Source: trusted client. Run `openssl s_client -starttls ldap -connect ldap.nova.a6.test:389 -verify_return_error -CAfile <CA-file>`. Expected: Verify return code 0 and SAN includes ldap.nova.a6.test.
ExpectedResult: LDAP certificate is issued by the local CA, contains SAN ldap.nova.a6.test, and validates without disabling certificate checks.

Subsection: OpenLDAP, PKI and SSSD identity services
Description: SSSD resolves LDAP identities on all three required hosts with no local Unix duplicates.
Commands: On each host run `getent passwd maya`, `getent passwd timur`, `id maya`, `id timur`, and `getent -s files passwd maya timur` (or inspect /etc/passwd). Expected: correct LDAP IDs/groups; no local copies.
ExpectedResult: sh-user-a6, ops-a6 and services-a6 resolve maya/timur and required groups from LDAP; no maya/timur records exist in the local files database.

Subsection: OpenLDAP, PKI and SSSD identity services
Description: PAM authentication using LDAP credentials works on the client host.
Commands: Source: sh-user-a6. Perform a safe PAM test using `pamtester`, local login, or equivalent approved method. Expected: authentication succeeds and SSSD is the identity/authentication backend.
ExpectedResult: maya can authenticate through PAM/SSSD on sh-user-a6 using Skill39@A6.

Subsection: OpenLDAP, PKI and SSSD identity services
Description: SSSD/LDAP clients enforce StartTLS and CA validation on all required hosts.
Commands: Inspect SSSD/LDAP client configuration on all three hosts and perform one verified `ldapsearch -ZZ` from each host. Expected: trusted TLS succeeds and no certificate-validation bypass is configured.
ExpectedResult: sh-user-a6, ops-a6 and services-a6 use LDAP TLS with trusted CA; TLS_REQCERT=never/insecure_skip_verify or equivalent bypass is absent.

Subsection: NFSv4 and SMB shared file services
Description: NFSv4 and SMB expose the same underlying dataset.
Commands: Source: services-a6. Run `exportfs -v` and `testparm -s`. Expected: both NFS export and [team] share resolve to /srv/files/team.
ExpectedResult: Both protocols use /srv/files/team; there is no duplicate/synchronized copy.

Subsection: NFSv4 and SMB shared file services
Description: POSIX ownership and default ACL enforce the required policy for existing and newly created objects.
Commands: Source: services-a6. Run `namei -l /srv/files/team` and `getfacl /srv/files/team`. Expected: effective ACL and default ACL/setgid design supports the task policy; confirm with temporary create/read tests.
ExpectedResult: filewriters has write; linuxusers has read. New files/directories inherit permissions without manual chmod/chown.

Subsection: NFSv4 and SMB shared file services
Description: NFSv4 export policy is correct.
Commands: Source: services-a6. Run `exportfs -v` and inspect NFS listener. Expected: permitted networks only, root_squash present, NFSv4 service active.
ExpectedResult: NFSv4 TCP/2049 export permits only 10.76.10.0/24 and 10.76.20.0/24 and uses root_squash.

Subsection: NFSv4 and SMB shared file services
Description: Shanghai client mounts the NFS share through the private/WireGuard path.
Commands: Source: sh-user-a6/sh-edge-a6. Mount or inspect the active mount; run `nfsstat -m` (or `mount`) and `ip route get 10.76.30.10` on sh-edge-a6. Expected: NFS version 4 and route via wg0.
ExpectedResult: sh-user-a6 accesses files.nova.a6.test via NFSv4 and the route to 10.76.30.10 is through wg0.

Subsection: NFSv4 and SMB shared file services
Description: SMB authentication/authorization policy matches the task.
Commands: Source: services-a6. Run `testparm -s`. Expected: effective share policy implements guest denial, linuxusers restriction and filewriters write rule. From a client, `smbclient -L //files.nova.a6.test -N` must not obtain guest share access.
ExpectedResult: Share [team] points to /srv/files/team; guest access is disabled; valid users are restricted to linuxusers; write is permitted only for filewriters.

Subsection: NFSv4 and SMB shared file services
Description: SMB authentication works for maya and timur using LDAP-backed Unix identities.
Commands: Source: services-a6/client. Confirm `getent passwd maya timur`; then run authenticated `smbclient` connections for both users. Expected: both can open/list the share; Unix identities are LDAP-backed.
ExpectedResult: maya and timur authenticate to [team] with Skill39@A6 while their Unix UID/GID comes from SSSD/LDAP.

Subsection: NFSv4 and SMB shared file services
Description: Cross-protocol visibility works in both directions with no copy/sync step.
Commands: Create two uniquely named temporary files as maya: one through the NFS mount and one through `smbclient`. Expected: each is immediately visible/readable through the other protocol. Remove test files after verification.
ExpectedResult: A file created by maya through NFS is immediately readable through SMB, and a file created by maya through SMB is immediately readable through NFS.

Subsection: NFSv4 and SMB shared file services
Description: maya and timur have the required effective permissions through both protocols.
Commands: Run a controlled permission matrix using temporary files through NFSv4 and SMB. Expected: every maya write operation succeeds and every prohibited timur write operation fails while timur read/list succeeds. No manual chmod/chown between protocol tests.
ExpectedResult: maya can create, modify, rename and delete via NFS and SMB. timur can list/read via both but cannot create, modify, rename or delete.
Notes: This higher-value aspect assesses the complete end-user file-access policy; award 0 or 0.75 only.

Description: HTTPS portal is available and contains the required page text.
Commands: Source: trusted internal client. Run `curl --cacert <CA-file> -fsS https://portal.nova.a6.test/`. Expected: HTTP 200 and required text.
ExpectedResult: https://portal.nova.a6.test/ returns HTTP 200 and contains NOVA A6 SERVICES.

Description: Web certificate validates and contains both required SAN names.
Commands: Run `openssl s_client -connect portal.nova.a6.test:443 -servername portal.nova.a6.test -verify_return_error -CAfile <CA-file>`. Expected: Verify return code 0 and both SAN names.
ExpectedResult: SAN contains portal.nova.a6.test and portal-public.nova.a6.test; chain validates to the local CA.

Description: HTTP redirects to HTTPS.
Commands: Run `curl -I http://portal.nova.a6.test/`. Expected: 3xx status and Location beginning `https://portal.nova.a6.test/`.
ExpectedResult: http://portal.nova.a6.test/ returns a 3xx redirect to the HTTPS URL.

Description: `/staff/` uses LDAP authentication over CA-validated StartTLS.
Commands: Inspect the active Apache auth configuration and CA/TLS settings; perform a successful maya authentication. Expected: LDAP/StartTLS path is used and no insecure validation bypass is present.
ExpectedResult: Apache authentication is backed by LDAP and certificate validation is not disabled.

Description: `/staff/` authorization follows webadmins membership.
Commands: Run three requests: anonymous, maya:Skill39@A6, timur:Skill39@A6. Expected: anonymous denied, maya 200, timur denied after authentication.
ExpectedResult: Anonymous is denied; maya receives HTTP 200; timur authenticates but is denied authorization.

Description: Postfix/Dovecot base mail configuration is correct.
Commands: Run `systemctl is-active postfix dovecot`, `postconf`, `doveconf`, and `ss -ltnp`. Expected: active services, local domain, Maildir and required listeners.
ExpectedResult: services-a6 serves nova.a6.test; Postfix and Dovecot are active; Maildir is used; listeners exist on 25, 587 and 993.

Description: SMTP TCP/25 accepts local-domain delivery without imposing an unstated STARTTLS requirement.
Commands: Source: internal client. Use `nc`/`telnet`/equivalent to TCP/25 and issue EHLO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO for timur@nova.a6.test. Expected: local recipient accepted. STARTTLS on port 25 is not required for this aspect.
ExpectedResult: A normal SMTP dialogue can submit mail to a valid local recipient according to the task policy.

Description: Submission TCP/587 requires TLS and authenticated submission.
Commands: Check EHLO capabilities on 587. Attempt submission without auth -> denied. Repeat with STARTTLS and maya credentials -> accepted for local recipient. Inspect active SASL/PAM/SSSD backend as needed.
ExpectedResult: STARTTLS is offered/required on 587; unauthenticated submission is not accepted; maya authentication succeeds using the required identity stack.

Description: IMAPS TCP/993 validates TLS and accepts LDAP-backed user credentials.
Commands: Use `curl --cacert <CA-file> --user <user>:Skill39@A6 imaps://mail.nova.a6.test:993/INBOX` for both users. Expected: TLS verification and login succeed.
ExpectedResult: maya and timur can authenticate to IMAPS; TLS certificate validation succeeds.

Description: Mail certificate contains both required SAN names.
Commands: Run `openssl s_client` against 993 (and/or 587 STARTTLS) with `-verify_return_error -CAfile <CA-file>`. Expected: Verify return code 0 and both SAN names.
ExpectedResult: SAN contains mail.nova.a6.test and mail-public.nova.a6.test and validates to the local CA.

Description: Mail is local-domain-only and the required message is delivered end-to-end.
Commands: First test RCPT to `user@example.invalid` on TCP/25 without auth and on 587 with authenticated maya: both must be rejected. Then send a unique A6-MAIL-TEST message via authenticated 587 and search/fetch it from timur INBOX via IMAPS. Expected: external relay denied in both cases and local message retrieved.
ExpectedResult: External recipient is rejected both without authentication and with authenticated Submission. maya sends subject A6-MAIL-TEST to timur via 587; timur retrieves it via IMAPS/993.

Description: nftables is persistent, stateful and default-deny.
Commands: Source: both gateways. Run `systemctl is-active/is-enabled nftables`, `nft list ruleset`, and a safe syntax check of the persistent ruleset. Expected: all required policies/state rule and no syntax error.
ExpectedResult: nftables active/enabled on both gateways; INPUT and FORWARD policy drop; established,related accepted; persistent ruleset loads without error.

Description: WAN ingress policy permits WireGuard but blocks direct DNS/LDAP exposure.
RunFrom: opposite WAN endpoint / sz-edge WAN context
Commands: Source: opposite WAN endpoint / sz-edge WAN context. Confirm working WireGuard handshake. Probe the gateway WAN address on 53/389. Expected: no DNS/LDAP service exposure.
ExpectedResult: UDP/51820 is reachable for the peer; WAN-address TCP/UDP 53 and TCP/389 are not exposed.

Description: Required private service flows are permitted without a broad any-any forwarding rule.
Commands: Run representative live private flows already defined in B/C/E and inspect the FORWARD chain. Expected: required flows work and no broad unconditional accept rule exists.
ExpectedResult: DNS, LDAP, HTTPS, mail and required ICMP work on intended private paths; no unconditional `accept` bypasses policy.

Description: NFSv4 and SMB are private-only at the firewall/NAT boundary.
Commands: From sh-user-a6 verify private NFS/SMB access. Then probe `198.18.76.20:2049` and `198.18.76.20:445`. Expected: private success; WAN-address probes fail.
ExpectedResult: Internal permitted clients can reach TCP/2049 and TCP/445; 198.18.76.20:2049 and :445 are not exposed from Shanghai/WAN.

Description: Monitoring ports are private-only.
Commands: From an internal permitted source verify required monitoring endpoints. From Shanghai/WAN path probe `198.18.76.20` on 3000, 9090, 9100, 9115. Expected: no WAN exposure.
ExpectedResult: Internal monitoring access works; WAN-address 3000/9090/9100/9115 is not exposed.

Description: SNAT uses the exact site WAN addresses.
Commands: For Shanghai, generate a permitted WAN-directed session and capture on sh-edge WAN; expected source 198.18.76.10. For Shenzhen, generate a permitted WAN-directed session from ops-a6 and capture on sz-edge WAN; expected source 198.18.76.20.
ExpectedResult: Shanghai private-to-WAN traffic is translated to 198.18.76.10; Shenzhen private-to-WAN traffic is translated to 198.18.76.20.

Description: Private WireGuard traffic is not SNATed.
Commands: Generate a private TCP connection sh-user-a6 -> services-a6. On services-a6 use `ss`, service log or `tcpdump` to inspect peer address. Expected: source 10.76.10.100, not a gateway/WAN address.
ExpectedResult: A Shanghai private connection reaching services-a6 retains original source 10.76.10.100.

Description: DNAT rules are exact and no prohibited services are published.
Commands: From sh-user-a6 connect to 198.18.76.20 ports 8443, 2587 and 2993 and verify the intended internal service is reached. Inspect `nft list ruleset` for exact translations and absence of prohibited DNAT mappings.
ExpectedResult: 8443->10.76.30.10:443; 2587->:587; 2993->:993 all work. No DNAT exists for LDAP, DNS, NFS, SMB, Prometheus, Grafana or exporters.

Description: Monitoring images are local-only and use the required tags.
Commands: On ops-a6 run `docker image inspect a6-prometheus:local a6-grafana:local` and `docker compose config`. Expected: both local tags and no build/external image reference.
ExpectedResult: a6-prometheus:local and a6-grafana:local exist; Compose does not use build: or external registry images.

Description: Compose defines exactly two application services/containers.
Commands: Run `docker compose config --services` and `docker compose ps`. Expected: exactly prometheus/grafana and exact container names.
ExpectedResult: Services are prometheus and grafana; containers are a6-prometheus and a6-grafana.

Description: Docker network, named volumes and restart policies are correct.
Commands: Run `docker network inspect a6-monitoring`, `docker volume inspect ...`, and `docker inspect` for mounts/restart policy. Expected: all required resources attached correctly.
ExpectedResult: Dedicated network a6-monitoring is used by both containers; a6-prometheus-data and a6-grafana-data are mounted to data paths; restart policy is unless-stopped.

Description: Both internal DNS servers are configured for the containers and internal names resolve.
Commands: Inspect Compose/container DNS settings for both addresses. Run `docker exec a6-prometheus getent hosts portal.nova.a6.test` and the equivalent in a6-grafana. Expected: both DNS servers configured and lookup succeeds.
ExpectedResult: Effective container DNS configuration includes 10.76.40.10 and 10.76.40.20; internal NOVA names resolve.

Description: Node Exporter is active/enabled on all three monitored servers.
Commands: On each server run `systemctl is-active` and `systemctl is-enabled` for the installed Node Exporter unit and verify listener 9100. Expected: active/enabled/listening on all three.
ExpectedResult: directory-a6, network-a6 and services-a6 run Node Exporter on TCP/9100 and it is enabled at boot.

Description: Prometheus scrapes itself and all three Node Exporters with the required interval and metrics.
Commands: Use Prometheus HTTP API/config endpoint. Expected: 15s interval; `up=1` for self + 3 node targets; required `node_*` metric families present for directory/network/services.
ExpectedResult: global scrape_interval=15s; self target and three node targets are up; CPU, memory, filesystem, load and uptime metrics exist for all three nodes.

Description: Blackbox Exporter is active/enabled and its modules match the required probe types.
Commands: Run `systemctl is-active/is-enabled` for Blackbox Exporter; inspect its loaded config. Expected: listener 9115, DNS query module and CA-validating HTTPS module.
ExpectedResult: ops-a6 runs Blackbox Exporter on 9115. DNS probes perform an actual DNS query; HTTPS probe validates the CA and does not set insecure_skip_verify.

Description: Prometheus receives successful Blackbox results for every required service target.
Commands: Query Prometheus `probe_success`. Expected: eight required service targets present and value 1 for each.
ExpectedResult: probe_success=1 for primary DNS, secondary DNS, LDAP, HTTPS, Submission, IMAPS, SMB and NFSv4, with distinguishable target/service labels.

Description: Grafana admin authentication works and self-sign-up is disabled.
Commands: Run `curl -u admin:Skill39-A6-Monitor! http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/user` -> HTTP 200. Repeat with wrong password -> HTTP 401. Inspect effective Grafana setting/API for `users.allow_sign_up=false`.
ExpectedResult: Correct admin credentials authenticate; an incorrect password is rejected; user self-sign-up is disabled.

Description: Prometheus datasource is automatically provisioned with exact settings.
Commands: Use Grafana API `/api/datasources/uid/prometheus-a6` and inspect provisioning file mounted from /opt/a6-monitoring. Expected: exact fields and provisioned origin.
ExpectedResult: Name Prometheus-A6; UID prometheus-a6; URL http://prometheus:9090; default=true.

Description: Dashboard is automatically provisioned with the required identity and refresh rate.
Commands: Use Grafana search/dashboard APIs and inspect dashboard provisioning. Expected: exact folder/title/UID and refresh not greater than 30s.
ExpectedResult: Folder A6; title A6 Integrated Infrastructure; UID a6-integrated-infra; refresh <=30s.

Description: Target Availability panel is correct and live.
Commands: Inspect dashboard JSON and open the live panel. Expected: query based on `up`; monitored targets have distinguishable labels and current values.
ExpectedResult: Panel uses `up` and distinguishes the monitored Prometheus/Node Exporter targets.

Description: Service Availability panel is correct and live.
Commands: Inspect dashboard JSON and live panel. Expected: query based on `probe_success`; all eight required services are distinguishable.
ExpectedResult: Panel uses `probe_success` and distinguishes primary DNS, secondary DNS, LDAP, HTTPS, Submission, IMAPS, SMB and NFSv4.

Description: CPU Utilization panel shows all three monitored Linux servers.
Commands: Inspect panel PromQL and live results. Expected: three distinguishable server series with non-empty current values.
ExpectedResult: directory-a6, network-a6 and services-a6 have live CPU utilization values.

Description: Available Memory panel shows all three monitored Linux servers.
Commands: Inspect panel PromQL and live results. Expected: three distinguishable server series and clear unit/meaning.
ExpectedResult: Memory is clearly represented as available amount or percentage for directory-a6, network-a6 and services-a6.

Description: Root Filesystem Usage panel shows `/` for all three monitored Linux servers.
Commands: Inspect panel PromQL and live results. Expected: mountpoint `/` and three distinguishable server series with current values.
ExpectedResult: Root filesystem usage is displayed for directory-a6, network-a6 and services-a6.

Description: Monitoring detects a real assessed service failure and recovery.
Commands: Choose SMB, HTTPS, LDAP or a mail TCP service. Record baseline `probe_success=1`, stop the service, wait up to two scrape intervals, expect 0; restart service, expect return to 1. Restore service before continuing.
ExpectedResult: Stopping one assessed service changes its corresponding probe_success from 1 to 0; restarting it returns to 1 within the configured probe/scrape cycles.

Description: Private and public-style application flows use the two intended network paths.
Commands: Run private HTTPS to portal.nova.a6.test and public-style HTTPS to 198.18.76.20:8443 from sh-user-a6. Use `ip route get` plus short captures on sh-edge wg0 and WAN. Expected: private flow on wg0; public-style flow on WAN only.
ExpectedResult: Internal portal/private service access from Shanghai uses WireGuard; portal-public:8443 uses the WAN path and DNAT, not wg0.

Description: Docker Compose down/up preserves monitoring data and provisioning without pulling images.
Commands: Before shutdown note a known historical Prometheus time range and verify Grafana objects by API. Execute the exact down/up commands. Expected: same named volumes, prior Prometheus history queryable, datasource and dashboard still present.
ExpectedResult: After `docker compose down` then `docker compose up -d --pull never`, historical Prometheus data remains and the Grafana datasource/dashboard still exist.

Description: Monitoring containers automatically recover after Docker service restart or ops-a6 reboot.
Commands: At the end of normal functional marking restart Docker, or perform a controlled ops-a6 reboot if permitted. Expected: both containers automatically running and ports 9090/3000 available.
ExpectedResult: a6-prometheus and a6-grafana return to running without manual `docker compose up`.

Description: Core infrastructure services are enabled and return active after controlled restart.
Commands: Check `systemctl is-enabled`/`is-active` for the defined service list. Perform controlled restarts by host/service group. Expected: every required service returns active; no undefined 'service group' scoring is used.
ExpectedResult: BIND primary/secondary, Kea, slapd, Apache, Postfix, Dovecot, NFS, Samba, Node Exporters and Blackbox Exporter are enabled where applicable and active after restart.
